what_its_for: Felodipine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering your blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It belongs to a group of medicines called calcium channel blockers, which help relax and widen your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or break the tablet, as this can cause too much medicine to be released at once and may be harmful. You can take felodipine with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can raise the level of the drug in your body to unsafe levels.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. The usual starting dose for adults is 5 mg once daily, taken in the morning. Your doctor may adjust your dose up to 10 mg or down to 2.5 mg depending on how your blood pressure responds. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first. Always take felodipine at the same time every day to keep your blood pressure under control.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Taking a double dose can cause your blood pressure to drop too low.
storage: Store felodipine tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container, away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past their expiration date. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice — they can cause dangerous levels of this medicine to build up in your body. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness or fainting. Be careful when getting up quickly from sitting or lying down, especially when you first start this medicine, as it may make you feel dizzy. Avoid activities that require full alertness, like driving, until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: severe dizziness or fainting, chest pain or rapid or irregular heartbeat, severe swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles, yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), or a fast or pounding heartbeat. Also call your doctor if you notice your blood pressure is still very high, you have a severe headache, or you have any serious side effects that worry you. Common mild side effects like flushing, headache, or minor ankle swelling may go away as your body adjusts, but still mention them to your doctor.
when_it_works: You may start to notice your blood pressure lowering within a few hours of taking your first dose. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use to see the full benefit of this medicine. It is very important to keep taking felodipine every day, even if you feel well, because high blood pressure often has no symptoms. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (over 65): You may be more sensitive to felodipine and may need a lower dose (starting at 2.5 mg per day). You may be at higher risk for dizziness and falls, so get up slowly from sitting or lying positions. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may start you on a lower dose because your body may process this medicine more slowly. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine is generally not recommended during pregnancy. Children: Felodipine is not currently approved for use in children. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed, but always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions.
